a monoclonal antibody was produced that reacted to a human cytomaegalovirus (HCV)-induced nuclear 68K protein.

a monoclonal antibody (Mab) reactive to a human cytomegalovirus (HCV)-induced nuclear 68K protein, which is expressed in various cells after viral infection or microinjection, is different from the major immediate early 72K protein.

the 68 K protein is expressed in cells infected with HMCV or in cells microinjected with cloned DNA, containing the major IE region, and that the 68 k protein is not a degradation or modification product of the 72 K protein.

the characterization of an IE protein which is not a modification product of major IE 72 K protein and is not expressed after infection of non-permissive cells.
the differential expression of the major IE protein in various cells after viral infection or microinjection.
the differential expression of the 68 and 72K nuclear proteins of HCMV.

the 68,000-molecular-weight protein (p68) was a novel product of the major immediate-early gene of HCMV.
the 68k protein is not the major immediate early protein of HCMV.
the major IE protein of HCMV is differentially expressed as two forms, the 72K and the 68K proteins, in various cell types and at various times after infection or microinjection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 68 K protein is a novel IE protein, distinct from the 72K nuclear protein, and that the 68 kDa protein is expressed in a variety of human cell types after infection or microinjection with HCMV DNA.
the 68 K protein is a novel IE protein of HCMV and that it may be a useful marker for HCMV IE gene expression.

the 68 K protein is a new IE protein of HCMV and that its expression is different from that of the major IE protein.
